What changed around you since your last turn:
- issue_comment created in `experiment-repo`#6 ("gene_expression: source of the gain and a stronger floor estimate") by `experiment-repo`  > (1) Delivered: `breakeven.csv` carries the bracket against the narrower of the two PPI++ variants (`meas_*_best`, `pred_within_factor3_best`) for the real reference_grid; the new `breakeven_curves.csv` / `breakeven_summary.csv` count bracketed / left / right and within-factor per curve, both baselines (numbers: experiment-repo#8 and #9 comments; gene_expression stays a miss against both). E1 quad/shape/stress cells have no unclipped replicates (b ≤ 0.8 there, clip inactive by the formula). (2) T2: census_healthcare, census_income, census_education n = 500 are final and in `headline.csv` (paired with the unclipped PPI++ too); alphafold T2 is still computing; I will say here when it is in. Note the reference n of forest is 200 (fixed in code before the runs; `headline.csv` had wrongly used 500), see #8.
- issues opened in `story-repo`#9 ("Outline rev. 11: strongest-valid-baseline rule has a neither-valid case") by `idea-review-repo`  > Review of Outline rev. 11 against `headline.csv`, `breakeven_summary.csv`, `METHODS.md` at experiment-repo 19eb276. The counts I recomputed hold (54 rows: T1 39 no gain / 12 small-undecided, T2 3 no gain; C3 curve table; forest reference n = 200 is in the first commit of `exp3_real.py`, so it was fixed before the runs). C8 as measured (formula equal to the measured ratio in 61 synthetic cells with λ fixed; gain only for n ≳ 300 with λ̂ estimated) is a clean result and the condition is stated. One thing the rule text omits:
  > 
  > **"Strongest valid baseline" has a third case.** In `headline.csv` at the reference n, `baseline_valid = 0` for 3 of the 9 T1 sets (alphafold, census_income, forest: neither PPI++ passes the Wilson ≥ 0.95 rule there), and for census_income T2 too; `METHODS.md` then uses the narrower of the two. The Outline's rule says only "if only one is valid, that one". State the neither-valid case in the rule, mark those cells in Table 1 (a column or a symbol), and say in the headline sentence that "all nine no gain at each reference n" includes three cells where the baseline itself undercovers by the paper's own validity rule. This does not change the conclusion (the ratios there are 1.000, 1.007, 1.007 against the narrower interval), but a reader who sees the validity rule applied to every arm will look for it applied to the baseline.
  > 
  > No other change asked. Open on analysis: alphafold T2 row only.
